memory_update.content: For AI Layer 3 chunks made entirely of high-attention reference names, cap underfollowed_discovery at 1 unless the company has a clearly niche, poorly understood, and testable hidden supply-chain signal.

Use AVGO, NVDA, ASML, ANET, and CRWV as reference demand and architecture anchors. The next Serenity layer should search one to two steps below them for optical components, advanced-packaging tools, probe cards, substrates, power delivery, liquid cooling, grid interconnection, and electrical balance-of-plant suppliers.

Key falsifiers for this reference chunk include hyperscaler capex cuts, AI cluster utilization weakness, margin compression from competition, power/interconnection delays, and evidence that bottlenecks migrate away from the mapped supplier nodes.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track AI networking/custom silicon backlog, customer concentration, AI revenue growth, custom ASIC design wins, and pull-through to optical modules, testing, substrates, and power components.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary-source verification from recent filings, earnings calls, and segment disclosures to quantify AI networking/custom silicon backlog and distinguish durable customer commitments from cycle-driven demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Broadcom is the strongest reference anchor in this chunk for AI networking silicon and custom accelerator demand. It helps map pull-through into optical modules, DSPs, substrates, packaging, test, retimers, connectors, and power delivery components. The Serenity value is less in Broadcom being underfollowed and more in using its backlog, AI revenue mix, and customer concentration as a demand signal for narrower suppliers beneath it.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is a mega-cap consensus AI infrastructure name. Underfollowed value, if any, is likely one or two layers below Broadcom in optical, packaging, test, substrate, or component suppliers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track whether demand constraints shift from accelerator availability to HBM, advanced packaging, power, cooling, networking, inference efficiency, or data-center interconnection.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current primary-source evidence on system-level bottlenecks, customer deployment constraints, and whether order timing is limited by NVIDIA supply or by downstream power, cooling, networking, and facility readiness.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: NVIDIA remains the dominant AI accelerator systems reference node. Its architectures drive demand across HBM, advanced packaging, substrates, networking, power, cooling, and data-center infrastructure. It scores highest on demand durability and bottleneck severity, but low on mispricing and underfollowed discovery because the market already treats it as the central AI beneficiary.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is the most visible AI infrastructure reference name. Its research use is to identify which second-order bottlenecks become more valuable as accelerator scarcity shifts toward memory, packaging, networking, power, or cooling.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track EUV and High-NA order timing, customer capex commitments, export-control effects, memory versus logic demand, and whether subsystem suppliers show stronger hidden leverage.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need updated order-book and customer capex evidence to separate AI-driven incremental demand from broader foundry, memory, and geopolitical capex cycles.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: ASML is a structural semiconductor equipment chokepoint for advanced-node logic and memory capacity that supports AI accelerators and HBM. It scores very high on bottleneck severity and supplier scarcity, but lower on Serenity priority than Broadcom and NVIDIA because its linkage to near-term AI system expansion is more mediated through semiconductor capex cycles and customer order timing.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is a widely owned and widely analyzed lithography reference bottleneck. The underfollowed hunt should move toward ASML subsystem suppliers, precision optics, motion-control components, inspection tools, materials, and service bottlenecks.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track AI cluster networking mix, hyperscaler concentration, Ethernet adoption versus InfiniBand, gross margin pressure, lead times, component bottlenecks, and optical module attach rates.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need primary evidence quantifying the AI networking portion of revenue and backlog, plus supplier-level evidence showing which components are capacity constrained.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Arista is a useful reference anchor for high-performance Ethernet networking in AI clusters. It is especially useful for testing the Ethernet-versus-InfiniBand architecture shift and for mapping demand into optical transceivers, cables, switch components, retimers, power supplies, and testing. Its bottleneck score is lower than NVIDIA, Broadcom, or ASML because equipment-level competition and customer design choices can shift faster than true physical chokepoints.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is a visible large-cap AI networking beneficiary. Its Serenity value is as a demand confirmation tool for underfollowed optical, component, and manufacturing-service suppliers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Track utilization, customer concentration, financing terms, power availability, GPU supply, data-center lease obligations, and whether capacity additions outpace demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need verified current evidence on utilization, contract duration, customer concentration, financing costs, and whether new capacity is constrained by power/interconnection or by end-demand quality.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: CoreWeave is a useful reference for AI compute-capacity demand and for tracing pressure into GPUs, data centers, power, networking, cooling, and financing markets. It ranks below the semiconductor and networking anchors because its bottleneck control is less clear: it depends on access to GPUs, power, data-center sites, customer contracts, and financing rather than owning a hard-to-replace component chokepoint.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed. It is a visible AI cloud infrastructure name. The more interesting Serenity angle is whether its expansion reveals hidden constraints in power availability, transformers, cooling, interconnection, data-center construction, or financing terms.

summary: This chunk is entirely a reference-anchor lane, not an underfollowed alpha lane. The highest Serenity priority goes to names that best map downstream chokepoints in AI networking, accelerators, semiconductor equipment, and data-center infrastructure. Because all candidates are high-attention large/mega-cap names, underfollowed_discovery and mispricing_potential are structurally capped. These names should primarily be used to trace second-order supplier opportunities rather than treated as hidden chokepoint candidates themselves.
